pictures.scene: Bouts, Christ in the House of Simon — Christ sits at the Pharisee's table in a dark blue robe with His hand raised to speak, the white cloth laid in front of Him with loaves, a glass and a fish on a pewter dish, while the bearded host in a jewelled cap and an olive gown leans in at His shoulder and watches Him without a word, and a woman in green and blue has gone down on the tiled floor at His feet and is drying them with her loosened hair, one sabbath, jesus went to eat in the home of a leading pharisee, and those in attendance were watching him closely, …
pictures.name: pd_bouts_christ_in_the_house_of_simon

pictures.scene: Murillo, Christ at the Pool of Bethesda — Christ stands at the top of the steps in a violet robe and a dark blue cloak, barefoot, looking down with His hand opened towards the sick man, while the paralytic lifts himself off the ground on his arms to answer Him and a second man sits on the stones below with a cloth tied round his head, the long colonnade of the pool runs away behind them with more of the sick lying along it in the shade, and an angel comes down through the cloud above the water, so jesus asked the experts in the law and the pharisees, is it lawful to heal on the sabbath or not, but they remained silent, then jesus took hold of the man, healed him, and sent him on his way, …
pictures.name: pd_murillo_pool_of_bethesda

pictures.scene: Potter, Cattle in a Meadow — the herd is lying out on the grass under the pollarded willows in the evening light with a white and red cow resting her head on the turf at the front, a dun cow stretched beside her and a big black ox standing over them with his horns up, a dark bull with a shaggy white face couched in the corner of the field, and away at the right a herdsman in a broad hat walks up with his stick on his shoulder and a little dog running at his heels to bring them in, and he asked them, which of you whose son or ox falls into a pit on the sabbath day will not immediately pull him out, and they were unable to answer these questions, …
pictures.name: pd_potter_drenken

pictures.scene: Bruegel, The Peasant Wedding — the whole barn is packed for the wedding feast with the bride sitting still under a paper crown and a green cloth hung on the wall behind her, her hands folded and her eyes down, while the guests crowd the long table on both sides drinking out of jugs and eating with their spoons, and two servers come straight down the front of the picture carrying a door taken off its hinges with ten bowls of porridge balanced on it, the one in a red cap and a white apron gripping the pole and looking back over his shoulder, when jesus noticed how the guests chose the places of honor, he told them a parable, when you are invited to a wedding banquet, do not sit in the place of honor, in case someone more distinguished than you has been invited, …
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_peasant_wedding

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, Haman Recognizes His Fate — the great man in a deep scarlet robe and a gold turban stands out of the darkness with his eyes lowered and his mouth shut, one hand laid flat on his chest and the other hanging open and empty at his side, while behind him at the right two bearded men in shadow watch him without a word as he is led away from the table where he had taken the high place, then the host who invited both of you will come and tell you, give this man your seat, and in humiliation, you will have to take the last place, …
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_haman_recognizes_his_fate

pictures.scene: Perov, The Refectory — a rich lady in a lilac silk gown sweeps into the vaulted hall on the arm of an old official with a star on his coat, and the whole room turns to watch her, a black robed monk bowing her in with his hand out and another leaning in at her shoulder, while a man lies flat on his face on the stone floor in front of her skirts and a ragged woman with two children on the ground at the right stretches up both hands and is not looked at, for everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and the one who humbles himself will be exalted, …
pictures.name: pd_perov_kloostermaaltijd

pictures.scene: Dusart, Street Musicians at the Inn Door — a poor old woman in a white cap and a patched blue apron stands playing a hurdy gurdy outside the thatched tavern with the handle turned in her hand, a boy in a yellow jacket bending into a pipe beside her and a smaller child in a broad hat crowding up behind him, while two men come out at the door to listen and the people of the house lean over the half door at the right, a bent old man in a black hat laughs over them, a barefoot girl in a kerchief holds onto a seated boy at the left and a dog lies down in the dust of the road, but when you host a banquet, invite the poor, the crippled, the lame, and the blind, and you will be blessed, …
pictures.name: pd_dusart_straatmuzikanten_bij_de_herberg

pictures.scene: Makovsky, A Boyar Wedding Feast — the guests are crowded along the table in the warm vaulted hall in heavy brocade and fur, and a white bearded old boyar in a gold sleeved coat half rises with a tall gold cup lifted in his hand and his mouth open to call out over the table, the bride in her pearled headdress and white veil sitting quiet behind him, a lady in a jewelled kokoshnik laughing at his shoulder, a stout lord in a flowered robe and a pearl cap turning round to answer him, and the gold plate of the house stacked up on a red cloth under the window, when one of those reclining with him heard this, he said to jesus, blessed is everyone who will eat at the feast in the kingdom of god, …
pictures.name: pd_makovsky_boyarenbruiloft

pictures.scene: Constable, The Cornfield — the lane runs up out of the shade between two great elms to a gate in the hedge, and beyond it the ripe corn stands yellow right across the field to the river and the church tower in the distance, with a reaper at work along the edge of it, a plough left lying by the bank, a flock of sheep coming down the sandy track with the dog standing in the middle of the road, a donkey and her foal in the grass under the trees, and a boy in a red waistcoat lying flat on his face at the little stream to drink, but one after another they all began to make excuses, the first one said, i have bought a field, and i need to go see it, please excuse me, …
pictures.name: pd_constable_the_cornfield

pictures.scene: Dupre, Cattle in the Limousin — a stand of great oaks and poplars goes up the right of the picture with the white heads of the summer cloud piled behind them and the blue coming through at the top, and down on the open grass at the left the cattle have been brought out to the pasture, a brown and white cow turning her horns towards us, a red ox standing over the ones that are lying down, a goat picking along the track, and a drover in a pale smock stands at the edge of the herd with a small boy at his side and a woman in a red bodice sitting on the ground behind the beasts, another said, i have bought five yoke of oxen, and i am going to try them out, please excuse me, …
pictures.name: pd_dupre_cattle_limousin

pictures.scene: Master of Alkmaar, Feeding the Hungry — the bread is being given out in the open street of the town, a woman in a white headcloth and a long apron holding a round basket of loaves out at the door of the house while a young man in a blue gown hands them on, and the poor of the place press in from the right to take them, a mother in green with a child reaching up at her side, an old man in a red cloak closing his hand on a loaf, a woman carrying a baby on her shoulder, and a crippled man dragging himself along the cobbles on his wooden blocks in front of them all with his face turned up, while Christ stands quietly among the crowd in the middle and a little dog sits in the empty street, go out quickly into the streets and alleys of the city, and bring in the poor, the crippled, the blind, and the lame, …
pictures.name: pd_alkmaar_barmhartigheid

pictures.scene: Ruisdael, The Road through the Oak Wood — a sandy track comes winding out of the trees towards us in the late afternoon, running between the heavy trunks of old oaks whose branches close right over the road, a dead bough hanging bare at the left and a torn stump lying in the grass at the right, with the one break of pale cloud showing through the leaves above the bend and the light reaching along the track and into the open field at the end of it, so the master told his servant, go out to the highways and hedges and compel them to come in, so that my house will be full, …
pictures.name: pd_ruisdael_weg

pictures.scene: van Eyck, The Adoration of the Lamb — the Lamb stands on a red draped altar in the middle of a green meadow with a ring of light about His head and His blood running into a golden cup, and the companies come in towards Him from every side over the grass, angels in white kneeling in a circle round the altar with the cross and the pillar held up behind them, two of them swinging censers on long chains, and in the near corners the prophets and the holy men kneel reading out of their books and looking up, with the fountain of living water playing into its stone basin in front and the towers of the city standing on the horizon, large crowds were now traveling with jesus, and he turned and said to them, …
pictures.name: pd_eyck_heirscharen

pictures.scene: El Greco, Christ Carrying the Cross — Christ holds the beam of the cross up against His shoulder with both hands, the one laid flat along the wood and the other open below it, and lifts His face towards the light with the crown of thorns pressed down on His head and the blood running from it onto His cheek and beard, His eyes wide and not in protest, wearing a crimson tunic under a deep blue cloak that falls across the whole front of the picture, with the stormy sky breaking white behind His head, and whoever does not carry his cross and follow me cannot be my disciple, …
pictures.name: pd_el_greco_christ_carrying_the_cross

pictures.scene: Bruegel, The Tower of Babel — the enormous tower stands half built on the rock above the town, its lower storeys finished in pale stone with their arches and balconies already weathering while the red brick upper rings are still open to the sky and leaning out of true, cranes and scaffolding and ladders left standing on every terrace, carts and tiny workmen crawling up the ramps, the sea and the ships showing far below at the right, and in the grass at the very front the masons are still cutting fresh blocks and dragging them up out of the quarry, otherwise, if he lays the foundation and is unable to finish the work, everyone who sees it will ridicule him, saying, this man could not finish what he started to build, …
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_the_tower_of_babel

pictures.scene: Holbein, The Ambassadors — the king's envoy stands at his full height in front of a green damask curtain in a black velvet gown lined with white fur and slashed pink satin sleeves, a gold chain and medal round his neck, one hand on his jewelled dagger and the other laid along the shelf beside him, and the whole apparatus of his embassy is set out on the two tables at his shoulder, a celestial globe, a quadrant and sundials above, a globe of the earth, an open book of arithmetic and a lute below, with the tiled pavement running away under his feet, and if he is unable, he will send a delegation while the other king is still far off, to ask for terms of peace, …
pictures.name: pd_holbein_the_ambassadors

pictures.scene: Sanchez Cotan, Quince, Cabbage and Melon — the back of the larder is pure black and the few plain things in it are lit as if nothing else in the world existed, a yellow quince with two leaves still on the stalk hanging on a thread at the top, a great green cabbage hung below it on a second thread with its outer leaves curling open, and a melon lying on the stone ledge with a wedge cut out of it so that the seeds and the wet flesh show, every rib and bloom of the rind painted out to the last mark, in the same way, any one of you who does not give up everything he has cannot be my disciple, salt is good, but if the salt loses its savor, with what will it be seasoned, …
pictures.name: pd_cotan_brood

pictures.scene: de Witte, The Oude Kerk in Amsterdam during a Sermon — the white vaults and the tall traceried windows of the old church go up out of the top of the picture and the daylight comes down through them onto the stone, the minister standing up in the little wooden pulpit against the pillar with his hands out and his mouth open, the elders seated in their hats along the panelling under him, and the people gathered down in the shadow at the front, a woman in a white collar holding her book, a small girl in a yellow jacket standing against her, a man leaning on the bench with his hat in his hand, two women in black on their chairs at the right, and a brown and white dog sitting in the patch of sunlight on the floor, it is fit neither for the soil nor for the manure pile, and it is thrown out, he who has ears to hear, let him hear, …
pictures.name: pd_de_witte_interior_of_the_oude_kerk_amsterdam_during_a_sermon

lines.text: One Sabbath, Jesus went to eat in the home of a leading Pharisee, and those in attendance were watching Him closely.
Right there before Him was a man with dropsy.
So Jesus asked the experts in the law and the Pharisees, Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath or not?
But they remained silent. Then Jesus took hold of the man, healed him, and sent him on his way.
And He asked them, Which of you whose son or ox falls into a pit on the Sabbath day will not immediately pull him out?
And they were unable to answer these questions.
When Jesus noticed how the guests chose the places of honor, He told them a parable:
When you are invited to a wedding banquet, do not sit in the place of honor, in case someone more distinguished than you has been invited.
Then the host who invited both of you will come and tell you, Give this man your seat. And in humiliation, you will have to take the last place.

But when you are invited, go and sit in the last place, so that your host will come and tell you, Friend, move up to a better place. Then you will be honored in front of everyone at the table with you.
For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and the one who humbles himself will be exalted.

Then Jesus said to the man who had invited Him, When you host a dinner or a banquet, do not invite your friends or brothers or relatives or rich neighbors. Otherwise, they may invite you in return, and you will be repaid.
But when you host a banquet, invite the poor, the crippled, the lame, and the blind,
and you will be blessed. Since they cannot repay you, you will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous.
When one of those reclining with Him heard this, he said to Jesus, Blessed is everyone who will eat at the feast in the kingdom of God.
But Jesus replied, A certain man prepared a great banquet and invited many guests.
When it was time for the banquet, he sent his servant to tell those who had been invited, Come, for everything is now ready.
But one after another they all began to make excuses. The first one said, I have bought a field, and I need to go see it. Please excuse me.
Another said, I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I am going to try them out. Please excuse me.
Still another said, I have married a wife, so I cannot come.

The servant returned and reported all this to his master. Then the owner of the house became angry and said to his servant, Go out quickly into the streets and alleys of the city, and bring in the poor, the crippled, the blind, and the lame.
Sir, the servant replied, what you ordered has been done, and there is still room.
So the master told his servant, Go out to the highways and hedges and compel them to come in, so that my house will be full.
For I tell you, not one of those men who were invited will taste my banquet.
Large crowds were now traveling with Jesus, and He turned and said to them,
If anyone comes to Me and does not hate his father and mother and wife and children and brothers and sisters, yes, even his own life, he cannot be My disciple.
And whoever does not carry his cross and follow Me cannot be My disciple.
Which of you, wishing to build a tower, does not first sit down and count the cost to see if he has the resources to complete it?
Otherwise, if he lays the foundation and is unable to finish the work, everyone who sees it will ridicule him,
saying, This man could not finish what he started to build.
Or what king on his way to war with another king will not first sit down and consider whether he can engage with ten thousand men the one coming against him with twenty thousand?
And if he is unable, he will send a delegation while the other king is still far off, to ask for terms of peace.
In the same way, any one of you who does not give up everything he has cannot be My disciple.
Salt is good, but if the salt loses its savor, with what will it be seasoned?
It is fit neither for the soil nor for the manure pile, and it is thrown out.
He who has ears to hear, let him hear.
